title: Host Execution Model and World Loop Reconstruction
confidence: medium-high for MBBSEmu host behavior; medium for Classic MajorMUD equivalence
canonical_rule: Librarium remains canonical. MBBSEmu and MMUD Explorer are external evidence only.

core_findings.claim: Player-visible module processing is host-driven, not client-side. Sessions in module state are serviced by host session loop callbacks such as STTROU, STSROU, and optional polling routines.
BEGIN_POLLING registers a per-channel routine that the host calls as often as possible until STOP_POLLING. This is a host polling mechanism, not modem latency itself.
TICKER is a shared exported global that increments once per second and is a plausible source for module time comparisons.
RTKICK callbacks are delayed by seconds and then executed once. RTIHDLR callbacks are approximately 18 Hz / ~55 ms. SYSCYC and INITASK provide additional repeated host-level callbacks.
Telnet/modem connection timing affects when bytes are received/flushed, but current evidence does not support treating network ping/latency as the authoritative gameplay tick.

timing_primitives.name: STSROU
timing_primitives.cadence: Status change or deferred processing; status code 240 or 5 per MBBSEmu comments

timing_primitives.name: BEGIN_POLLING
timing_primitives.cadence: As fast/often as possible while registered

timing_primitives.name: RTIHDLR
likely_consumers: interrupt-level real-time handlers; not yet proven for MajorMUD gameplay

timing_primitives.name: SYSCYC
timing_primitives.cadence: host cycle callback if module pointer set

not_proven: Whether MajorMUD uses TICKER, RTKICK, STSROU, SYSCYC, RTIHDLR, BEGIN_POLLING, or a combination for each gameplay subsystem.
Exact output flush ordering relative to combat/regen/AI/quest updates.
That modem ping directly drives gameplay state changes.
